title: Transient promotional quota & pricing override PRD (feature-flag driven)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Add a structured, auditable mechanism for short-lived promotional pricing and quota overrides that product and GTM can enable without engineering deploys. Promotions include temporary free trial quota boosts, time-limited discounted per-token rates, and scenario-based rate-limit relaxations for campaigns. The system must integrate with billing, metering, console visibility, and entitlement enforcement across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
requirements: Promotion config model: name, id, scope (account/org/caller), start_ts, end_ts, quota_delta (tokens or calls), rate_multiplier (decimal), rate_limit_patch (per-caller concurrency or rps), priority (int), rollback_policy
Feature-flag driven activation: promotions are activated via the Redwood console and exposed to runtime via a lightweight feature flag service and a cached promotion catalog on serving nodes.
Entitlement enforcement: runtime must apply quota_delta and rate_limit_patch at request-evaluation time; promotions should be additive to existing entitlements and traceable to a promotion id.

Metering & billing integration: metered usage must record both gross and net (post-promo) units, persist promotion id on metering events, and surface a clear invoice line item for promotion discounts or free-credit consumption.
Idempotent grant semantics: applying the same promotion twice (e.g., repeated activation calls, race conditions) must not double-count quota or apply duplicate discounts.

Transactional rollback: if a promo is canceled mid-window, the system must support immediate cessation for enforcement and either prorated reversal for future billing or a one-time credit adjustment; manual and automated rollback flows must be supported.

Audit trail & reporting: every promotion action (create/update/activate/deactivate/rollback) must create an auditable event linked to user id, timestamp, and affected accounts; console must show per-account promo usage and projected invoice impact.
Canary & scoped rollout: promotions can be targeted to a percent sample of accounts and/or specific account lists to support beta campaigns.
Backward compatibility: when promotions are not present, current quota/rate limit and billing behavior must be unchanged.
Compliance & privacy: promo metadata must not expose other customers' PII and must respect data residency settings for customers on Private deployments.
non_goals: Replace full promo marketing stack (e.g., coupon codes on billing portal) — this is for engineering-triggered / console-driven short-term technical promos.
Complex multi-step funnel discounting (e.g., multi-line item invoices with tiered stacking across months).
Automated ML-based promo targeting — targeting will be explicit lists/percentages only.
Changing core rate sheet model — promotions are overlays on top of existing rates, not new fundamental pricing tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Create promotion in Console: PO/marketing can define a promotion with start/end, scope, quota_delta or rate_multiplier — console form validates fields and shows simulated invoice impact.
Activation path: toggling Activate publishes the promotion to feature-flag service and serving nodes within < 60s in hosted mode (document expected propagation window).

Runtime enforcement: within propagation window, a promoted account receives additional quota (quota_delta) and altered per-token rate (rate_multiplier) and observed in token-level logs with promotion id.

Metering rows: all metering events include two fields: promotion_id (nullable) and billed_units (post-promo). Reports using billing export display original_units, discount_amount, and final_amount per invoice line.
Idempotency: re-applying the same promotion manifest does not increase allocated quota; automated test demonstrates idempotent grant across 10 repeated activation requests.

Rollback behavior: canceling an active promotion stops new enforcement within propagation window and generates a billing adjustment event; manual credit issuance via billing UI is possible and linked to the promotion id.
Analytics: console shows promotion usage heatmap and projected invoice delta; a dashboard query (promotions_usage_v1) returns per-account consumed promo units and remaining promo quota.
Security review: architecture doc and data flows reviewed and signed off by Security; export of promotion audit events respects privacy requirements for Private customers.
Integration tests: end-to-end tests exist that validate promotion lifecycle in staging for hosted and a documented runbook for Dedicated/Private deployments to apply promotion catalogs.
Docs & runbooks: engineering runbook for emergency revoke and billing team's playbook for issuing credits are published and linked from PRD.
risks: Billing mismatch risk if metering and promotion application are out of sync — mitigation: atomic write of promotion_id on metering event and nightly reconciliation job.
Promotion abuse (sharing of promo-enabled credentials) — mitigation: tie scoped promotions to account id and optionally to caller origins/IP with rate limiting.
Propagation lag on Dedicated/Private deployments could lead to inconsistent enforcement — mitigation: documented expected latency and a CLI to push catalog updates to private runtimes.
Complex rollback accounting creating invoice disputes — mitigation: clear UI messaging, automated credit issuance with promotion id, and customer support playbook.
